title: Raw rational diagram and conditional exact-heart descent
statement: Fix finite-field data D [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], ell different from its characteristic, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_ell, a finite map f:X->Y of separated finite-type D.k-schemes, and y:Spec D.k->Y. Let G be normalized Geometry [def-zl-finite-restriction-geometric-comparisons] and I an IntegralComparisons system [def-zl-finite-restriction-integral-diagram] satisfying Laws and Coherent. Let N be Endpoints G I satisfying ScalarNormalized [def-zl-finite-restriction-normalization], so the integral beta comparisons are the canonical geometric ones. There exists R:RationalComparisons I [def-zl-finite-restriction-coefficient-descent-data] with the specified literal integral-object and tensor-Hom formulas and actual exchange and restriction components. The rational direct image of G satisfies DirectImageDescent with exactly its inverse-theta scalar comparisons. Each R.diagram q satisfies HeartExactDescent [def-zl-finite-restriction-finite-data]: assuming its stages preserve both standard halves, its descended functor has an additive exact heart restriction with the literal object and map formulas. This is only rationalization and exact-heart passage; no normalized integral geometry or finite-data theorem is asserted.

proof.text: Given normalized geometry G and an integral comparison system I satisfying Laws and Coherent, raw rational transport tensors the actual integral functors and two transformations with scalars. Their localized object, map, component and beta equations give RationalComparisons. The inverse-theta direct-image comparison is a stage-system Morphism by the inverse of the rational direct-image cocycle in G.Normalized.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2); rationalization and point-section normalization.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] to each rational functor family and to both compatible restriction transformations. Steps 2–5 verify its identity and tower equations. Explicitly, for $\Phi_E$ with comparison $\beta_{L/E}:T_{L/E}\Phi_E\simeq\Phi_LT_{L/E}$, a common-stage representative $u:K_L\to K'_L$ is sent to
$$[L,\beta_{L/E'}^{-1}\Phi_L(u)\beta_{L/E}].$$
The cited node proves independence of both the representative and common field, and descends equations of compatible transformations and their composites. These are exactly the pair categories of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; the Karoubi extension offered by the abstract lemma is unused. This proves descent of the actual maps, not merely existence of some isomorphic functors.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(1); common-stage functors and specified arrows.

proof.text: For the last, conditional assertion, use [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations] for the bounded standard structures and t-exact scalar transitions; Step 1's category identification makes its finite and pair conventions precisely ours. A stagewise t-exact direct-image family with the comparisons already proved satisfies [lem-a1-texact-pair-descent], which gives exactness and t-exactness of the descended functor. Alternatively its preservation of each half follows immediately by representing an object in that half at one finite stage and applying that stage's functor. For the exact heart restriction use [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4): a short exact sequence in the common-stage heart is a distinguished triangle; its image remains distinguished and all three objects remain in the heart, hence the image sequence is short exact. This proves the claimed retention of exactness without assuming faithfulness of scalar transition maps. Apply this to each of the three rationalized functors and to the direct-image family; exactness uses their inherited normalized shifts and localized distinguished triangles. The full-subcategory heart restriction has the literal object/map formulas, so gives HeartExactDescent. Preservation of halves by representing an object at one stage gives the direct-image TExactDescent. No t-exactness is asserted without the stagewise antecedent. The input Endpoints.ScalarNormalized identifies the three integral beta maps with geometric scalar comparisons; this supplies normalized shift compatibility rather than assuming it for arbitrary natural isomorphisms.

theorem finiteRestrictionRationalAssembly
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsFinite f]
    (y : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ Y)
    (G : Geometry l Ω f y) (I : IntegralComparisons l f y Ω)
    (N : Endpoints l Ω f y G I)
    (hG : G.Normalized) (hI : I.Laws) (hcI : I.Coherent) (hN : N.ScalarNormalized) :
    ∃ R : RationalComparisons l f y Ω I,
      DirectImageDescent l f y Ω G ∧
        ∀ q : Vertex, HeartExactDescent l Ω X (R.diagram q)
